ov: A tree-dwelling marsupial of eastern and southern Australia, and not a bear. It lives on eucalyptus leaves, a diet so low in energy that koalas sleep up to 20 hours a day.
rg: Eucalyptus woodland in coastal eastern and southern Australia: Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria and South Australia.
df: Almost entirely eucalyptus leaves, which are low in nutrients and contain toxins that put off most other mammals.

cf.tip: Its closest living relative, the wombat, lives on the ground in burrows it digs with powerful claws, not up in trees.

fx: Males mark their presence with scent from a gland on their chest.
notes: Since 2022 the koala is listed as Endangered in Queensland, New South Wales and the ACT; the IUCN status is Vulnerable. The existing fact (sleeps 20 hours) is confirmed.
